name: Kroger
description: Kroger is the largest supermarket operator in this batch: 2,697 supermarkets, 2,250 pharmacies and 1,731 fuel centers in 35 states and DC, plus online delivery and pickup, and 33 food plants (bakeries and dairies) that make about 20 percent of its private-label units. It has one reportable segment. Money comes from selling groceries at a thin margin: operating profit was 1.28 percent of sales in fiscal 2025 after a $2.5B write-down of its automated online-order fulfillment centers, and about 2.6 percent in fiscal 2024. About 25 percent of sales is fresh food, 52.5 percent other groceries and household goods, 12.3 percent pharmacy and 9.2 percent fuel. Two things lift profit above the store margin: private label (Our Brands, over $39B of sales) and what Kroger calls alternative profit streams (described in the 10-K as using retail data and traffic; composition not extracted), $1.5B of operating profit in 2025 versus adjusted FIFO operating profit of $4.9B.

gics.note: SEC SIC code 5411 (Retail-Grocery Stores). Kroger's reported segment is one (retail operations), but 12.3% of sales is pharmacy and 9.2% is fuel, and its filing names CVS and Walgreens in its stock-performance peer group next to Walmart, Costco and Target.

hq.note: 1014 Vine Street, Cincinnati, OH 45202 (SEC EDGAR business address)

employees.note: 'More than 403,000 full- and part-time' associates (FY2025 10-K; text truncated in extract). Wikipedia infobox shows 414,000 (2023).

businessLines.name: Retail operations (Kroger's only reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Shoppers pay at the register for groceries, prescriptions and fuel, in stores and online, at a low margin. The 10-K also points to two profit levers: its own brands (Our Brands) and 'alternative profit streams', which it says use the data and traffic generated by its retail business. Identical sales excluding fuel rose 2.9% in 2025, driven by eCommerce, Pharmacy and Fresh.
businessLines.description: Supermarkets and multi-department stores, pharmacies, fuel centers, fulfillment centers and online ordering across the US, plus food manufacturing for its own stores.

revenue.note: Fiscal year ended 2026-01-31; +0.4% vs FY2024. Sales to retail customers without fuel $132,712M (+1.3%), supermarket fuel $13,584M (-9.3%), other $1,346M. Q2 2026 (12 weeks ended 2026-08-15) $34,621M vs $33,940M.

operatingProfit.note: GAAP operating profit, after $2.5B of fulfillment network impairment and related charges; FY2024 $3,849M. Adjusted FIFO operating profit $4.9B (+5% vs 2024). Q2 2026 $971M vs $863M; 28-week YTD 2026 $2,378M vs $2,185M.
